rows.text: For machinery in the categories listed in Annex I, Part A, the manufacturer must apply one of the Article 25(2) procedures: EU type-examination (module B) with internal production control (module C), full quality assurance (module H), or unit verification (module G).

rows.text: A safety component with fully or partially self-evolving behaviour falls under Annex I, Part A, point 5. Point 6 also covers embedded self-evolving machine-learning systems that ensure safety functions, but only in respect of those systems.

Under Annex III point 1.3.8.1 of the Regulation and Annex I point 1.3.8.1 of the Directive, guards for moving transmission parts must be interlocking movable guards where frequent access is envisaged. Otherwise, either fixed guards or interlocking movable guards may be used.

value: Risks related to moving parts
rows.text: Essential health and safety requirement 1.3.7 of Annex III addresses risks related to moving parts.

rows.value: The natural or legal person who carries out the substantial modification is considered the manufacturer and is subject to the Article 10 manufacturer obligations (Art. 18), provided the modification affects the safety of only machinery or a related product that is part of an assembly of machinery; a non-professional user modifying machinery for own use is excluded.
rows.text: Under Article 18 of the Regulation, the natural or legal person carrying out a substantial modification is treated as the manufacturer and must meet the Article 10 obligations, where the modification affects only the safety of machinery or a related product forming part of an assembly of machinery. A non-professional user modifying machinery for their own use is not considered a manufacturer.

rows.text: Until 2027-01-20 the Directive 2006/42/EC governs: machinery placed on the market must be accompanied by the EC declaration of conformity (Art. 5(1), and Art. 7(1) where it bears the CE marking), and by instructions in the required language, namely the instruction manual and the original instructions (or an accompanied translation) under Annex I, 1.7.4 and 1.7.4.2. Where the machinery is not assembled on the manufacturer's premises, the necessary instructions for performing the measures under Annex I, 4.4.2 must also accompany it.

The manufacturer must keep the technical documentation and the EU declaration of conformity for at least 10 years after the machinery or related product has been placed on the market or put into service (Art. 10(3) of the Machinery Regulation; see also Art. 12(2)).
Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 applies from 20 January 2027 (corrigendum point 10). Certain Articles apply earlier, from the dates set out in the corrigendum for those Articles.

Yes. Under the corrigendum point 6, machinery placed on the market in conformity with Directive 2006/42/EC before 20 January 2027 is allowed, and the Directive is only repealed from 20 January 2027 (point 5). On 16 January 2027 it can still be placed on the market.

rows.text: Under DM 2011, art. 2, c. 1, the first periodic verification of Annex VII work equipment is carried out by INAIL. Under D.Lgs. 81/2008 as amended (art. 71, c. 13), the periodic verifications must be carried out within twelve months.
The employer must keep the results of the checks under art. 71, paragraph 8 of D.Lgs. 81/2008 for at least the last three years (art. 71, c. 9).

The relevant dates are in the Corrigendum: the Directive is repealed from 20 January 2027 (point 5), the Regulation applies from that date (point 10), and products placed on the market under the Directive before then are covered by point 6.

They do show that the Regulation applies from 20 January 2027 (Corrigendum point 10) and that Directive 2006/42/EC is repealed from that date (Corrigendum point 5); the procedure for RC-5 would follow from its Annex I Part A or Part B category under Article 25.

rows.text: Four Annex I, Part A categories of the Regulation are not in Annex IV of Directive 2006/42/EC: removable mechanical transmission devices including their guards (point 1), portable cartridge-operated fixing and other impact machinery (point 4), safety components with fully or partially self-evolving behaviour (point 5), and machinery with embedded self-evolving ML systems ensuring safety functions (point 6). Vehicle servicing lifts (point 3) do appear in Annex IV, so they are excluded.

No. After 20 January 2027 the Machinery Regulation applies, and vehicle servicing lifts are an Annex I Part A point 3 category, so internal production control (module C) must be followed by EU type-examination (module B) under Article 25(2); the Directive's internal-checks route for Annex IV machinery is repealed by then.

rows.text: The Regulation adds the essential requirement in Annex III, point 1.1.9, on protection against corruption. It requires that software and data critical for compliance, and hardware components linked to them, be adequately protected against accidental or intentional corruption, and that evidence of legitimate or illegitimate intervention be collected and kept available. The Directive has no equivalent.

The facts do not establish which verification interval applies to IGEA device 8 (overhead travelling crane). Under Allegato VII of D.Lgs. 81/2008 the interval depends on whether the crane is fixed or mobile, its capacity above 200 kg, its use pattern and its age. Those conditions are not given for device 8, so the interval (annual P1Y, biennial P2Y or triennial P3Y) cannot be determined.

The truck-mounted hydraulic crane (built 2017, regular use, over 200 kg, not hand-operated, mobile) must be verified every two years under Allegato VII, riga 13 of D.lgs. 81/2008 as reflected in the facts, because its build year is not earlier than 10 years before today.

rows.value: Il soggetto che effettua le verifiche periodiche successive alla prima è, in generale, l'Azienda sanitaria nazionale (Asl) o l'Agenzia regionale protezione ambientale (Arpa) o i soggetti pubblici o privati abilitati; per le attrezzature dell'Allegato VII di particolare pericolosità, personale specializzato dell'ASP competente o un Organismo privato riconosciuto, e per le attrezzature dell'Allegato VII di proprietà o in comodato d'uso, il Corpo nazionale dei vigili del fuoco.
rows.text: After the first periodic verification, subsequent verifications are normally performed by the ASL, ARPA or authorised public or private bodies (inail-guide). For the Annex VII equipment with particular hazards, the competent ASP specialised staff or a recognised private body perform them, and for Annex VII equipment owned or on comodato d'uso the Corpo nazionale dei vigili del fuoco perform the comma 11 verifications (art. 71, c. 13-bis, D.Lgs. 81/2008).

The first periodic verification must be carried out within 45 days of receipt of the complete request, as set by Art. 71(11) of Legislative Decree 81/2008 and the INAIL guide. The sixty-day figure attributed to the 2011 Ministerial Decree does not appear in the provided facts; that decree's only stated term there is thirty days, for subsequent verifications.

No. Under the e-Series requirement, the UR5e, as a partly completed machine, shall only be put into service after being integrated into a final complete machine, and a risk assessment is required before it is placed into operation.

The nanoScan3 protective device must be tested at least once a year (regular tests, per the manual's p. 50 and p. 51, including the resolution detection test and the thorough check of the principal function). A daily visual check of the machine and protective device is also recommended in many cases.

The provided facts do not state how much notice a verifier must give IGEA when planning the checks. They only give 45-day deadlines for the employer's request to INAIL and for INAIL's first periodic verification after a complete request.

Under Allegato VII of the DLgs (riga 18) and the INAIL guide (p. 34), a fixed, regularly used lifting device over 200 kg built less than 10 years ago, such as device 13 built in 2017, must be checked every three years. The facts do not confirm the crane's fixed type or usage sector, which could change this to a biennial check.

The facts do not say whether this overhead travelling crane is fixed or mobile/transferable, or how it is used. Under Allegato VII (righe 13-16) that determines whether it needs annual or biennial verification in November 2028, since it will be more than 10 years old by then.

Under the Allegato VII rule for construction-site lifts and platforms guided vertically (DLgs 81/2008, Allegato VII, riga 11), an elevating platform must be verified every year, so the HINOWA device at position 24 needs an annual check. This assumes the platform is vertically guided, which the facts do not state directly.

The facts do not establish the verification interval for the DEMAG overhead crane at IGEA position 8 (it is a bridge crane per fact 3), nor its last verification date, so whether it is overdue cannot be determined from the provided material. The applicable interval in Allegato VII depends on load capacity, fixed or mobile type, use sector and manufacture year, none of which are given.
Replacing the UR5e (reach 850 mm) with the UR10e (reach 1300 mm) increases the reach by 450 mm, per the manufacturer reach specifications in the ur5e-manual and ur10e-manual.
The wear indicator of the load nut on the MA STAR 3.5 A lift must be checked every 6 months (MA STAR manual, p. 34). It must also be checked when the wear limit is reached.
